Application Fee Waiver
Fee Waiver Form
The form to request an application fee waiver is included in the payment section of the online application. To be considered, applicants need to select the waiver payment option and upload any required supporting documents before submitting the online application.
Credit: Keegan Houser
Eligibility
U.S. citizens or current permanent residents may be eligible for an application fee waiver.
There are two ways in which you may qualify for an application fee waiver:
You can demonstrate financial need, or
You have participated in certain programs that qualify for a fee waiver
Once you complete the Biographical Information and Personal Background sections of the application, the fee waiver will automatically appear in the Payment / Fee Waiver section if you are eligible.
Undocumented students (AB540 & non-AB540) may be considered for an application fee waiver if they demonstrate financial need. Visit Prospective Undocumented Graduate Students for additional information.
1. Financial Need
Financial need is determined by the Student Aid Index (SAI) number listed on your FAFSA Student Aid Report (SAR), or by the Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) on your tax return. To be eligible for the Fee Waiver:
SAI cannot exceed $6,655
Annual family income cannot exceed the maximum AGI listed in the Family Income Guidelines chart below.
FAMILY SIZE (including student)
FAMILY INCOME (Maximum AGI on Tax Return)
1
$29,526
2
$40,034
3
$50,542
4
$61,050
5
$71,558
For each additional family member
add $10,508
Required Documentation to Demonstrate Financial Need
To demonstrate financial need, enter the SAI or AGI on the Payment/Fee Waiver page of the graduate application and upload one of the following items:
A statement of need from a financial aid officer at the college or university that you are currently attending. This statement must include your Student Aid Index (SAI), the financial aid officer’s signature, and your signature verifying that the information reported is correct.
A photocopy of your 2027 – 2028 Student Aid Report (SAR). The SAR is generated from the information you provide on your Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) (https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa) form and includes your Student Aid Index (SAI). Do not submit a copy of your FAFSA.
A copy of your 2025 Federal Income Tax return. Provide either your Form 1040, if listed as an independent, or a copy of your parent’s or guardian’s 2025 Federal Income Tax return, if listed as a dependent.
Please redact all Social Security numbers before submitting these documents.
2. Program Participation
Participants in the following programs must submit verification of program participation, such as a letter bearing the original signature of the program director or adviser, or a copy of the current contract. Please upload your program verification to the Payment/Fee Waiver Page in the application.
A program-by-program review was conducted, prior to application going live on September 21, 2026, to confirm that program participation is open to all.

Application Fee Exemption Eligibility
The following categories of applicants are exempt from paying an application fee. If you are applying to any of these programs, “Fee Exemption” will automatically be selected in the payment section of the online application:
Health and Medical Sciences Joint Degree (UCSF)
You are applying to the HMS Joint Degree program
Optometry Residency Program
You are applying to the Optometry Residency Program at the School of Optometry
Education Abroad Program
You are applying for Course Work Only status through the EAP
